subject: MAP cadence — contingency stitching and timeline salvage
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood-inference.com>
To: Dana Patel <dana.patel@healthsphere.com>; HealthSphere Procurement <procurement@healthsphere.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP cadence — contingency stitching and timeline salvage

Hi Dana / procurement team,

Thanks again for the transparency on the legal and procurement timing — I know the team is working through the redlines. We tracked the MAP commitments against the evaluation milestones and see a 2–3 week drift in the sign-off path. Rather than push a single hard reset, I'd like to propose a short contingency stitch for the MAP so we can preserve delivery scope while we work through paperwork. High level: 

- Short-term split: allow an initial limited pilot (feature subset) to go live on dedicated capacity by 6/04 to validate performance and telemetry.
- MAP update: formalize a 3-week rebaseline window for acceptance criteria and procurement sign-off, target new close date 2026-06-18 (soft-lock until legal clears).
- Risk register: Redwood will add two mitigation lanes (capacity escrow + fallback to open model) if any procurement gating remains unresolved.

I've attached an updated MAP workbook (HealthSphere_MAP_v3.xlsx) with the proposed gates and ownership. Please review the pilot scope table (tab: pilot-slice) and call out any blockers. If this approach is acceptable we can loop in your procurement lead and push a short exec decision (Jordan and Kimberly are available to present options).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Confirm whether procurement can sign a pilot SOW with a limited clause (we can offer a 30-day audit window).
2) If yes, we finalize pilot SOW and pick a pilot go/no-go by 5/14.
3) If procurement requires full contract redline resolution first, please share the redline summary and we'll prepare the escalation pack.

Thanks — happy to run a 20-minute call this week to walk the MAP cells.

—
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood-inference.com
(415) 555-0192
Attachments: HealthSphere_MAP_v3.xlsx (Excel workbook, 83KB)
From: Dana Patel <dana.patel@healthsphere.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: HealthSphere Procurement <procurement@healthsphere.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP cadence — contingency stitching and timeline salvage

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the pragmatic options. A few updates from our side: legal has pushed back on the proposed data residency clause and wants explicit language for audit access; procurement is not comfortable authorizing a pilot SOW without a narrowed liability paragraph. That is likely to add ~2 weeks to our internal review.

We are open to a pilot approach but need your legal team to sign off on a short, limited SOW template. Can Redwood provide a one-page pilot addendum that isolates liability and data handling for the pilot environment? If so, I can move procurement faster.

Also copying Priya (VP Product) to keep execs aware — Priya, we discussed preserving the evaluation momentum with a limited pilot. Soojin proposed a 6/04 pilot start.

Dana Patel
Dir, Partnerships & Product Strategy
HealthSphere
Dana.Patel@healthsphere.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>
To: Dana Patel <dana.patel@healthsphere.com>, HealthSphere Procurement <procurement@healthsphere.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood-inference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP cadence — contingency stitching and timeline salvage

Hi Dana — thanks, this is helpful context.

We can provide a one-page pilot addendum that narrows liability, limits data exposure, and defines acceptance telemetry for the pilot. I've attached our SOC2 excerpt and vendor answers that specifically call out data handling controls; legal has pre-approved a limited pilot SOW template for cases like this (see attached: SOC2-vendor-answers.pdf).

To make the MAP and timeline concrete, here is a short risk log entry (to be appended to the MAP workbook):

- Risk ID: R-17
- Description: Procurement redlines delay pilot SOW approval, introducing a 2-week slip to evaluation window.
- Likelihood: Medium
- Impact: High (delays final close; impacts planned cutover and acceptance metrics)
- Mitigation: Provide pilot addendum (owner: Redwood legal); offer 30-day limited indemnity cap for pilot; run pilot on dedicated pool to isolate production data.
- Contingency: If procurement does not sign pilot by 5/14, escalate to execs and invoke credit holdback option.

Proposed rebaseline schedule (short):
- 2026-05-14: Pilot addendum signed (target)
- 2026-06-04: Pilot start (limited subset)
- 2026-06-18: Evaluation complete, handoff decision for full go-live

If HealthSphere agrees we will: (a) publish the updated MAP workbook with the R-17 entry, (b) create a mutual action checklist with names and dates, and (c) prepare a one-slide exec decision brief for any escalation.

Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Success — Enterprise
kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com
Attachments: SOC2-vendor-answers.pdf (PDF, 120KB)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>
To: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@healthsphere.com>, Dana Patel <dana.patel@healthsphere.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood-inference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Escalation: decision needed to preserve MAP momentum

Priya / Dana — quick note from Redwood leadership side. We want to make this as low-friction as possible but we need a go/no-go on the pilot addendum by Friday 5/14 to keep the evaluation window intact. If HealthSphere cannot sign the pilot addendum by then, we will need an explicit extension of the MAP timeline and a brief on which acceptance gates you want deferred. Impacts: engineering earmark will be released on 5/18 if no pilot commitment is received.

We can offer a one-time limited credit (2 weeks of committed capacity at no charge) if you sign the pilot addendum by 5/14 and agree to a short risk acceptance note to be stored in the MAP workbook. That is our path to preserve the 6/04 pilot start and evaluation cadence.

Can you confirm today whether Priya / procurement can commit to the 5/14 decision? If helpful, Jordan or Kimberly can jump on a 15-minute exec call this afternoon.

—
Jordan Blake
Head of Sales — West
jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com
(415) 555-0124
From: Dana Patel <dana.patel@healthsphere.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood-inference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Escalation: decision needed to preserve MAP momentum

Jordan / Soojin / Kimberly — we discussed internally and procurement will accept the pilot addendum approach. Priya has authorized the exec acceptance of the limited indemnity for the pilot. We will: 

1) Sign the pilot addendum by 5/14.
2) Commence the pilot on 6/04 as described in the MAP workbook.
3) Complete evaluation and provide acceptance decision by 6/18.

Please send the one-page pilot addendum and the DocuSign envelope and we'll route through procurement first thing tomorrow. Appreciate the credit offer — we'll take the offer under the terms you outlined.

Dana Patel
Dir, Partnerships & Product Strategy
HealthSphere
Attachments (forwarded): DocuSign request placeholder
